    def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map the first two unit coordinates along the two edges.

    A single instant is appended to every point. A time range uses the third unit
    coordinate.

    Args:
        unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

    Returns:
        Points on the parallelogram, with time appended when this rectangle has a
        time axis.

    """
    # Spatial transformation
    pt = self.origin + unit_samples[..., 0:1] * self.edge1 + unit_samples[..., 1:2] * self.edge2

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Add constant time dimension
        t = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)
    elif self.times is not None:
        # Add time range
        t = self.tmin + unit_samples[..., 2:3] * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)

    return pt

    class Box(Shape, ABC):
    """A parallelepiped spanned by three edges from ``origin``.

    Attributes:
        origin: Corner where the three edges meet.
        edge1: First edge.
        edge2: Second edge.
        edge3: Third edge.
        times: Time range, or ``None`` when the box has one instant or no time.

    """

    origin: Array
    edge1: Array
    edge2: Array
    edge3: Array
    times: Time | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        origin: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge1: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge2: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge3: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        times: Time | float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the corner, the three edges, and the optional time.

        A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
        [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

        Args:
            origin: Corner where the three edges meet.
            edge1: First edge.
            edge2: Second edge.
            edge3: Third edge.
            times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.origin = jnp.array(origin)
        self.edge1 = jnp.array(edge1)
        self.edge2 = jnp.array(edge2)
        self.edge3 = jnp.array(edge3)
        self.spatial_dims = self.origin.size
        self.dims = self.origin.size

        # Handle different time specifications
        if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
            # Single time instant
            self.single_time = float(times)
            self.times = None
            self.dims += 1
        elif isinstance(times, Time):
            # Time range
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = times
            self.tmin = times.min
            self.tmax = times.max
            self.tstep = times.step
            self.dims += 1
        else:
            # No time dimension
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = None

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the volume from the scalar triple product of the three edges.

        Returns:
            The absolute volume as a scalar array.

        """
        return jnp.abs(jnp.dot(self.edge1, jnp.cross(self.edge2, self.edge3)))

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the box around the eight corners.

        A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

        Returns:
            The lower and upper bounds.

        """
        # Compute all 8 corners, then min/max
        corners = jnp.stack(
            [
                self.origin,
                self.origin + self.edge1,
                self.origin + self.edge2,
                self.origin + self.edge3,
                self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2,
                self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge3,
                self.origin + self.edge2 + self.edge3,
                self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2 + self.edge3,
            ],
        )
        lower = jnp.min(corners, axis=0)
        upper = jnp.max(corners, axis=0)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time point
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Time range
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.tmin])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.tmax])])

        return lower, upper

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool | None = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the box through the oriented-bounding-box domain.

        ``show_normals`` and ``normal_scale`` are accepted and not used.

        Args:
            show_normals: Ignored. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Ignored. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Figure to draw on. Default: a figure created by the domain.
            ax: Axes to draw on. Default: axes created by the domain.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        """
        domain = SpatialDomain.from_obb(
            self.origin,
            self.edge1,
            self.edge2,
            self.edge3,
            times=self.times,
        )

        fig, ax = domain.draw(show=show, fig=fig, ax=ax)

        return fig, ax

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map the first three unit coordinates along the three edges.

        A single instant is appended to every point. A time range uses the fourth unit
        coordinate.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

        Returns:
            Points in the parallelepiped, with time appended when this box has a time axis.

        """
        # Spatial transformation
        pt = (
            self.origin
            + unit_samples[..., 0:1] * self.edge1
            + unit_samples[..., 1:2] * self.edge2
            + unit_samples[..., 2:3] * self.edge3
        )

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Add constant time dimension
            t = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
            pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Add time range
            t = self.tmin + unit_samples[..., 3:4] * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
            pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)

        return pt

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
        """Return a grid count from the three edge lengths.

        Each edge contributes at least two points, from its length divided by
        ``value``. The three counts are multiplied. A time range multiplies again by
        its step count, also at least two. One instant does not.

        Args:
            value: Spacing along each edge.

        Returns:
            The sample count.

        """
        len1, len2, len3 = (
            jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1),
            jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2),
            jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge3),
        )
        n_space = (
            jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len1 / value), 2)
            * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len2 / value), 2)
            * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len3 / value), 2)
        )

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
            return int(n_space)
        if self.times is not None:
            # Time range - multiply by time samples
            n_time = jnp.maximum(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep), 2)
            return int(n_space * n_time)
        return int(n_space)

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        n1 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1) / value)), 2)
        n2 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2) / value)), 2)
        n3 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge3) / value)), 2)

        if self.times is not None:
            n_time = max(int(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep)), 2)
            return n1, n2, n3, n_time

        return n1, n2, n3

    def __init__(
    self,
    origin: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
    edge1: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
    edge2: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
    edge3: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
    times: Time | float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Store the corner, the three edges, and the optional time.

    A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
    [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

    Args:
        origin: Corner where the three edges meet.
        edge1: First edge.
        edge2: Second edge.
        edge3: Third edge.
        times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

    """
    super().__init__()
    self.origin = jnp.array(origin)
    self.edge1 = jnp.array(edge1)
    self.edge2 = jnp.array(edge2)
    self.edge3 = jnp.array(edge3)
    self.spatial_dims = self.origin.size
    self.dims = self.origin.size

    # Handle different time specifications
    if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
        # Single time instant
        self.single_time = float(times)
        self.times = None
        self.dims += 1
    elif isinstance(times, Time):
        # Time range
        self.single_time = None
        self.times = times
        self.tmin = times.min
        self.tmax = times.max
        self.tstep = times.step
        self.dims += 1
    else:
        # No time dimension
        self.single_time = None
        self.times = None

    bounds() -> tuple[Array, Array]

    Return the box around the eight corners.

    A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

    The lower and upper bounds.

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
    """Return the box around the eight corners.

    A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

    Returns:
        The lower and upper bounds.

    """
    # Compute all 8 corners, then min/max
    corners = jnp.stack(
        [
            self.origin,
            self.origin + self.edge1,
            self.origin + self.edge2,
            self.origin + self.edge3,
            self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2,
            self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge3,
            self.origin + self.edge2 + self.edge3,
            self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2 + self.edge3,
        ],
    )
    lower = jnp.min(corners, axis=0)
    upper = jnp.max(corners, axis=0)

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Single time point
        lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
        upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
    elif self.times is not None:
        # Time range
        lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.tmin])])
        upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.tmax])])

    return lower, upper

    def draw(
    self,
    *,
    show_normals: bool = False,
    normal_scale: float = 1.0,
    fig: Figure | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    show: bool | None = True,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Draw the box through the oriented-bounding-box domain.

    ``show_normals`` and ``normal_scale`` are accepted and not used.

    Args:
        show_normals: Ignored. Default: ``False``.
        normal_scale: Ignored. Default: ``1``.
        fig: Figure to draw on. Default: a figure created by the domain.
        ax: Axes to draw on. Default: axes created by the domain.
        show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    """
    domain = SpatialDomain.from_obb(
        self.origin,
        self.edge1,
        self.edge2,
        self.edge3,
        times=self.times,
    )

    fig, ax = domain.draw(show=show, fig=fig, ax=ax)

    return fig, ax

    estimate_nsamples(value: float) -> int

    Return a grid count from the three edge lengths.

    Each edge contributes at least two points, from its length divided by value. The three counts are multiplied. A time range multiplies again by its step count, also at least two. One instant does not.

    Parameters:

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
    """Return a grid count from the three edge lengths.

    Each edge contributes at least two points, from its length divided by
    ``value``. The three counts are multiplied. A time range multiplies again by
    its step count, also at least two. One instant does not.

    Args:
        value: Spacing along each edge.

    Returns:
        The sample count.

    """
    len1, len2, len3 = (
        jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1),
        jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2),
        jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge3),
    )
    n_space = (
        jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len1 / value), 2)
        * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len2 / value), 2)
        * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len3 / value), 2)
    )

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
        return int(n_space)
    if self.times is not None:
        # Time range - multiply by time samples
        n_time = jnp.maximum(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep), 2)
        return int(n_space * n_time)
    return int(n_space)

    def measure(self) -> Array:
    """Return the volume from the scalar triple product of the three edges.

    return jnp.abs(jnp.dot(self.edge1, jnp.cross(self.edge2, self.edge3)))

    def residuals(self, ops: DifferentialOperators) -> Array:
    """Calculate the residual values for all collocation points.

    Evaluation uses the bound [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual].

    Args:
        ops: A [`DifferentialOperators`][pinnjax.DifferentialOperators] object.


    Returns:
        residuals: Array of residual values for each collocation point.

    Raises:
        InputError: If no collocation points have been generated for this Shape.
        InputError: If no [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual]
            has been bound to this Shape.

    """
    samples = self.samples
    if samples is None:
        msg = "There are no samples associated with this shape. Call .sample() first."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)
    residual_function = self.residual_function
    if residual_function is None:
        msg = (
            "There is no residual function associated with this shape. "
            "Call .set_residual() first."
        )
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)
    return residual_function(samples, ops)

    def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map the first three unit coordinates along the three edges.

    A single instant is appended to every point. A time range uses the fourth unit
    coordinate.

    Args:
        unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

    Returns:
        Points in the parallelepiped, with time appended when this box has a time axis.

    """
    # Spatial transformation
    pt = (
        self.origin
        + unit_samples[..., 0:1] * self.edge1
        + unit_samples[..., 1:2] * self.edge2
        + unit_samples[..., 2:3] * self.edge3
    )

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Add constant time dimension
        t = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)
    elif self.times is not None:
        # Add time range
        t = self.tmin + unit_samples[..., 3:4] * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)

    return pt

    class Hypercube(Shape):
    """A box in parameter space, sampled through one marginal per axis.

    ``lower`` and ``upper`` are the bounds used for the domain, the measure, and
    the default uniform marginals. A marginal maps the unit interval to that axis
    during ``transform``. There is no time axis.

    Attributes:
        lower: Lower bound of each axis.
        upper: Upper bound of each axis.
        axis_names: Name of each axis. Default names are ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
        marginals: Distribution used to map each unit-interval coordinate.
        evaluator: Callable run on the samples after ``sample``, or ``None``.
        evaluated_values: Array returned by the last ``evaluate`` call that stored
            its result, or ``None``.

    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        lower: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] | Array,
        upper: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] | Array,
        *,
        axis_names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
        marginals: tuple[MarginalSpec, ...] | None = None,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the bounds and one marginal per axis.

        Omitted marginals are uniform on each ``[lower, upper]`` interval. Omitted
        axis names are ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.

        Args:
            lower: Lower bound of each axis.
            upper: Upper bound of each axis. Each entry must be strictly greater than
                the matching entry of ``lower``.
            axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
            marginals: One marginal per axis. Default: a uniform distribution on each
                bound interval.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, applied to the samples at
                the end of ``sample``. Default: ``None``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the bounds differ in length, an upper bound is not strictly
                greater than the matching lower bound, or a name or marginal sequence
                does not have one entry per axis.

        """
        super().__init__()

        self.lower = jnp.asarray(lower, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        self.upper = jnp.asarray(upper, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        self.evaluator = evaluator
        self.evaluated_values = None

        if self.lower.shape != self.upper.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lower and upper must have the same length, "
                f"got {self.lower.shape} and {self.upper.shape}.",
            )

        if jnp.any(self.upper <= self.lower):
            raise ValueError("Each upper bound must be strictly greater than lower.")

        k = int(self.lower.shape[0])
        self.spatial_dims = k
        self.dims = k
        self.times = None

        if axis_names is None:
            self.axis_names = tuple(f"mu{i}" for i in range(k))
        else:
            if len(axis_names) != k:
                raise ValueError(f"axis_names length must be {k}")
            self.axis_names = tuple(axis_names)

        if marginals is None:
            self.marginals = tuple(
                _uniform_on_interval(
                    (float(self.lower[i]), float(self.upper[i])),
                )
                for i in range(k)
            )
        else:
            if len(marginals) != k:
                raise ValueError(f"marginals length must be {k}, got {len(marginals)}")
            self.marginals = tuple(marginals)

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the hypercube when it has at most three dimensions.

        Args:
            show_normals: Ignored.
            normal_scale: Ignored.
            fig: Figure to draw on. A new figure is created when omitted.
            ax: Existing axes. New axes are created when omitted.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If the supplied axes does not match the hypercube dimension.

        """
        del show_normals, normal_scale

        if self.dims > THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            config.LOGGER.warning(
                f"Cannot draw a {self.dims}D Hypercube. Only up to 3D is supported.",
            )
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)

            return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

        if self.dims == 1:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
            elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 1D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

            ax.plot(
                [self.lower[0], self.upper[0]],
                [0.0, 0.0],
                color="black",
                marker="o",
            )
            ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
            ax.set_yticks([])

        elif self.dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
            elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 2D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

            x0, y0 = self.lower
            x1, y1 = self.upper
            x = jnp.array([x0, x1, x1, x0, x0])
            y = jnp.array([y0, y0, y1, y1, y0])

            ax.plot(x, y, color="black", marker="o")
            ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
            ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")

        elif self.dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

            if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 3D Hypercube requires a 3D axes.")

            x0, y0, z0 = self.lower
            x1, y1, z1 = self.upper

            vertices = jnp.array(
                [
                    [x0, y0, z0],
                    [x1, y0, z0],
                    [x1, y1, z0],
                    [x0, y1, z0],
                    [x0, y0, z1],
                    [x1, y0, z1],
                    [x1, y1, z1],
                    [x0, y1, z1],
                ],
            )

            edges = (
                (0, 1),
                (1, 2),
                (2, 3),
                (3, 0),
                (4, 5),
                (5, 6),
                (6, 7),
                (7, 4),
                (0, 4),
                (1, 5),
                (2, 6),
                (3, 7),
            )

            for i, j in edges:
                edge = vertices[jnp.array([i, j])]
                ax.plot(edge[:, 0], edge[:, 1], edge[:, 2], color="black")

            ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
            ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
            ax.set_zlabel(self.axis_names[2])
            ax.set_box_aspect([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

        if show:
            plt.show()

        assert ax is not None
        return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

    @property
    def domain(self) -> Domain:
        """Return the bounds and axis names as a [`Domain`][pinnjax.Domain]."""
        return Domain(
            min=tuple(float(x) for x in self.lower.tolist()),
            max=tuple(float(x) for x in self.upper.tolist()),
            axis_names=self.axis_names,
        )

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the lower and upper bounds."""
        return self.lower, self.upper

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map unit-cube coordinates onto the marginal for each axis.

        The last axis of ``unit_samples`` is one coordinate per dimension, in ``[0, 1]``.
        An interval marginal maps that coordinate linearly onto its interval. A discrete
        marginal picks a value by cutting ``[0, 1]`` into equal bins. A continuous
        marginal uses its percent-point function.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Coordinates in the unit cube, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

        Returns:
            Points in parameter space, with the same shape as ``unit_samples``.

        """
        u = jnp.asarray(unit_samples, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        u_np = np.asarray(u)

        cols = [_transform_axis(u_np[..., i], self.marginals[i]) for i in range(self.dims)]
        return jnp.asarray(np.stack(cols, axis=-1), dtype=config.get_dtype())

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the volume of the bounding box.

        This is the product of ``upper - lower``. It does not depend on the marginals.

        Returns:
            The volume as a scalar array.

        """
        return jnp.prod(self.upper - self.lower)

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
        """Return how many points a uniform grid at this spacing would contain.

        Each axis uses at least two points. The count on an axis is the edge length
        divided by ``value``, rounded, and the counts are multiplied.

        Args:
            value: Spacing between grid points, in the same units as the bounds.

        Returns:
            The product of the per-axis counts.

        """
        edges = self.upper - self.lower
        per_axis = jnp.maximum(jnp.round(edges / value), 2)
        return int(jnp.prod(per_axis))

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        edges = self.upper - self.lower
        return tuple(max(int(jnp.round(edge / value)), 2) for edge in edges)

    def sample(
        self,
        method: SamplingMethod,
        sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        descriptor_count: int = 32,
    ) -> tuple[Array, int]:
        """Draw collocation points, then run ``evaluator`` when one was stored.

        Sampling follows [`Shape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.sample]. A stored evaluator
        is then applied with ``overwrite=True``, which replaces ``evaluated_values``.
        ``descriptor_count`` is ignored.

        Args:
            method: Sampler used to draw the points.
            sampling_values: Size passed to ``method``. ``None`` uses ``1000``.
            overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
            descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

        Returns:
            samples: Collocation points stored on this shape.
            n_points: Number of those points.

        """
        del descriptor_count
        self.samples, self.n_points = super().sample(
            method,
            sampling_values,
            overwrite=overwrite,
        )

        if self.evaluator is not None:
            self.evaluated_values = self.evaluate(self.evaluator, overwrite=True)

        return self.samples, self.n_points

    def evaluate(
        self,
        evaluator: SampleEvaluator | Sequence[SampleEvaluator],
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
    ) -> Array:
        """Apply one or more callables to the stored samples.

        Each callable is mapped over the sample rows. One callable returns that array.
        Several callables are stacked on a new leading axis. ``overwrite`` stores the
        result on ``evaluated_values``.

        Args:
            evaluator: One callable, or a sequence of callables. Each callable takes one
                sample row and returns an array.
            overwrite: Replace ``evaluated_values`` with the result. Default: ``False``.

        Returns:
            The mapped values, or a stack of those values when more than one callable
            was given.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``sample`` has not been called, or the sequence is empty.
            TypeError: If an entry in the sequence is not callable.

        """
        samples = self.samples
        if samples is None:
            raise ValueError("Shape must first be sampled prior to evaluation.")

        if isinstance(evaluator, Sequence):
            evaluators = tuple(evaluator)
        else:
            evaluators = (evaluator,)

        if len(evaluators) == 0:
            raise ValueError("evaluator sequence must contain at least one callable.")

        if not all(callable(fn) for fn in evaluators):
            raise TypeError("All evaluators must be callable.")
        values = [jnp.asarray(jax.vmap(fn)(samples), dtype=config.get_dtype()) for fn in evaluators]

        if len(values) == 1:
            out = values[0]
        else:
            out = jnp.stack(values, axis=0)

        if overwrite:
            self.evaluated_values = out
        return out

    @classmethod
    def from_domain(
        cls,
        domain: Domain,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> Hypercube:
        """Build a hypercube from the minimum, maximum, and axis names of a domain.

        Args:
            domain: Domain that supplies the bounds and axis names.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
                Default: ``None``.
            **kwargs: Forwarded to [`Hypercube`][pinnjax.Hypercube]. Use this for ``marginals``.

        Returns:
            A hypercube with those bounds and names.

        """
        return cls(
            lower=jnp.asarray(domain.min),
            upper=jnp.asarray(domain.max),
            axis_names=domain.axis_names,
            evaluator=evaluator,
            **kwargs,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_intervals(
        cls,
        *intervals: tuple[float, float],
        axis_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
    ) -> Hypercube:
        """Build a hypercube with a uniform marginal on each interval.

        Each pair is ``(lower, upper)``. The upper value must be strictly greater than
        the lower value.

        Args:
            *intervals: One ``(lower, upper)`` pair per axis.
            axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
                Default: ``None``.

        Returns:
            A hypercube whose bounds are those intervals.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If an interval is empty or reversed, or ``axis_names`` does not
                have one entry per interval.

        """
        specs = [_uniform_on_interval(iv) for iv in intervals]
        return cls.from_distributions(
            *specs,
            axis_names=axis_names,
            evaluator=evaluator,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_distributions(
        cls,
        *specs: MarginalSpec,
        confidence: float = 0.99,
        axis_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
    ) -> Hypercube:
        """Build a hypercube whose bounds come from one marginal per axis.

        An interval marginal uses its own endpoints. A discrete marginal uses the
        smallest and largest value. A continuous marginal uses its support when that
        support is finite. Otherwise, the bounds are the central ``confidence``
        probability interval.

        Args:
            *specs: One marginal per axis.
            confidence: Central probability used when a continuous support is infinite.
                Default: ``0.99``.
            axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
                Default: ``None``.

        Returns:
            A hypercube with those marginals and the derived bounds.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a derived upper bound is not strictly greater than the lower
                bound, or ``axis_names`` does not have one entry per marginal.
            TypeError: If a specification is not an interval, discrete, or continuous
                marginal.

        """
        lowers, uppers, marginals = [], [], []

        for spec in specs:
            lo, hi, marginal = _bounds_from_spec(spec, confidence)
            lowers.append(lo)
            uppers.append(hi)
            marginals.append(marginal)

        return cls(
            lower=jnp.asarray(lowers),
            upper=jnp.asarray(uppers),
            axis_names=tuple(axis_names) if axis_names else None,
            marginals=tuple(marginals),
            evaluator=evaluator,
        )

    def draw(
    self,
    *,
    show_normals: bool = False,
    normal_scale: float = 1.0,
    fig: Figure | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    show: bool = True,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Draw the hypercube when it has at most three dimensions.

    Args:
        show_normals: Ignored.
        normal_scale: Ignored.
        fig: Figure to draw on. A new figure is created when omitted.
        ax: Existing axes. New axes are created when omitted.
        show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the supplied axes does not match the hypercube dimension.

    """
    del show_normals, normal_scale

    if self.dims > THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
        config.LOGGER.warning(
            f"Cannot draw a {self.dims}D Hypercube. Only up to 3D is supported.",
        )
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111)

        return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

    if self.dims == 1:
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
        elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
            raise TypeError("A 1D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

        ax.plot(
            [self.lower[0], self.upper[0]],
            [0.0, 0.0],
            color="black",
            marker="o",
        )
        ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
        ax.set_yticks([])

    elif self.dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
        elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
            raise TypeError("A 2D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

        x0, y0 = self.lower
        x1, y1 = self.upper
        x = jnp.array([x0, x1, x1, x0, x0])
        y = jnp.array([y0, y0, y1, y1, y0])

        ax.plot(x, y, color="black", marker="o")
        ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
        ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
        ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")

    elif self.dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

        if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
            raise TypeError("A 3D Hypercube requires a 3D axes.")

        x0, y0, z0 = self.lower
        x1, y1, z1 = self.upper

        vertices = jnp.array(
            [
                [x0, y0, z0],
                [x1, y0, z0],
                [x1, y1, z0],
                [x0, y1, z0],
                [x0, y0, z1],
                [x1, y0, z1],
                [x1, y1, z1],
                [x0, y1, z1],
            ],
        )

        edges = (
            (0, 1),
            (1, 2),
            (2, 3),
            (3, 0),
            (4, 5),
            (5, 6),
            (6, 7),
            (7, 4),
            (0, 4),
            (1, 5),
            (2, 6),
            (3, 7),
        )

        for i, j in edges:
            edge = vertices[jnp.array([i, j])]
            ax.plot(edge[:, 0], edge[:, 1], edge[:, 2], color="black")

        ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
        ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
        ax.set_zlabel(self.axis_names[2])
        ax.set_box_aspect([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

    if show:
        plt.show()

    assert ax is not None
    return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
    """Return how many points a uniform grid at this spacing would contain.

    Each axis uses at least two points. The count on an axis is the edge length
    divided by ``value``, rounded, and the counts are multiplied.

    Args:
        value: Spacing between grid points, in the same units as the bounds.

    Returns:
        The product of the per-axis counts.

    """
    edges = self.upper - self.lower
    per_axis = jnp.maximum(jnp.round(edges / value), 2)
    return int(jnp.prod(per_axis))

    def evaluate(
    self,
    evaluator: SampleEvaluator | Sequence[SampleEvaluator],
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> Array:
    """Apply one or more callables to the stored samples.

    Each callable is mapped over the sample rows. One callable returns that array.
    Several callables are stacked on a new leading axis. ``overwrite`` stores the
    result on ``evaluated_values``.

    Args:
        evaluator: One callable, or a sequence of callables. Each callable takes one
            sample row and returns an array.
        overwrite: Replace ``evaluated_values`` with the result. Default: ``False``.

    Returns:
        The mapped values, or a stack of those values when more than one callable
        was given.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sample`` has not been called, or the sequence is empty.
        TypeError: If an entry in the sequence is not callable.

    """
    samples = self.samples
    if samples is None:
        raise ValueError("Shape must first be sampled prior to evaluation.")

    if isinstance(evaluator, Sequence):
        evaluators = tuple(evaluator)
    else:
        evaluators = (evaluator,)

    if len(evaluators) == 0:
        raise ValueError("evaluator sequence must contain at least one callable.")

    if not all(callable(fn) for fn in evaluators):
        raise TypeError("All evaluators must be callable.")
    values = [jnp.asarray(jax.vmap(fn)(samples), dtype=config.get_dtype()) for fn in evaluators]

    if len(values) == 1:
        out = values[0]
    else:
        out = jnp.stack(values, axis=0)

    if overwrite:
        self.evaluated_values = out
    return out

    @classmethod
def from_distributions(
    cls,
    *specs: MarginalSpec,
    confidence: float = 0.99,
    axis_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
) -> Hypercube:
    """Build a hypercube whose bounds come from one marginal per axis.

    An interval marginal uses its own endpoints. A discrete marginal uses the
    smallest and largest value. A continuous marginal uses its support when that
    support is finite. Otherwise, the bounds are the central ``confidence``
    probability interval.

    Args:
        *specs: One marginal per axis.
        confidence: Central probability used when a continuous support is infinite.
            Default: ``0.99``.
        axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
        evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
            Default: ``None``.

    Returns:
        A hypercube with those marginals and the derived bounds.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a derived upper bound is not strictly greater than the lower
            bound, or ``axis_names`` does not have one entry per marginal.
        TypeError: If a specification is not an interval, discrete, or continuous
            marginal.

    """
    lowers, uppers, marginals = [], [], []

    for spec in specs:
        lo, hi, marginal = _bounds_from_spec(spec, confidence)
        lowers.append(lo)
        uppers.append(hi)
        marginals.append(marginal)

    return cls(
        lower=jnp.asarray(lowers),
        upper=jnp.asarray(uppers),
        axis_names=tuple(axis_names) if axis_names else None,
        marginals=tuple(marginals),
        evaluator=evaluator,
    )

    @classmethod
def from_intervals(
    cls,
    *intervals: tuple[float, float],
    axis_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
) -> Hypercube:
    """Build a hypercube with a uniform marginal on each interval.

    Each pair is ``(lower, upper)``. The upper value must be strictly greater than
    the lower value.

    Args:
        *intervals: One ``(lower, upper)`` pair per axis.
        axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
        evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
            Default: ``None``.

    Returns:
        A hypercube whose bounds are those intervals.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If an interval is empty or reversed, or ``axis_names`` does not
            have one entry per interval.

    """
    specs = [_uniform_on_interval(iv) for iv in intervals]
    return cls.from_distributions(
        *specs,
        axis_names=axis_names,
        evaluator=evaluator,
    )

    return residual_function(samples, ops)

    def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Draw collocation points, then run ``evaluator`` when one was stored.

    Sampling follows [`Shape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.sample]. A stored evaluator
    is then applied with ``overwrite=True``, which replaces ``evaluated_values``.
    ``descriptor_count`` is ignored.

    Args:
        method: Sampler used to draw the points.
        sampling_values: Size passed to ``method``. ``None`` uses ``1000``.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on this shape.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    self.samples, self.n_points = super().sample(
        method,
        sampling_values,
        overwrite=overwrite,
    )

    if self.evaluator is not None:
        self.evaluated_values = self.evaluate(self.evaluator, overwrite=True)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map unit-cube coordinates onto the marginal for each axis.

    The last axis of ``unit_samples`` is one coordinate per dimension, in ``[0, 1]``.
    An interval marginal maps that coordinate linearly onto its interval. A discrete
    marginal picks a value by cutting ``[0, 1]`` into equal bins. A continuous

    """
    u = jnp.asarray(unit_samples, dtype=config.get_dtype())
    u_np = np.asarray(u)

    cols = [_transform_axis(u_np[..., i], self.marginals[i]) for i in range(self.dims)]
    return jnp.asarray(np.stack(cols, axis=-1), dtype=config.get_dtype())
